solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Men do it haphazardly around start of weekend in leisurely period?

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters wrap round the next piece
done haphazardly, the letters of these three words are thrown into a new order
start of takes just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A wry remark about what men get up to, carelessly, around the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haphazardly' scrambles MENDOIT into DO_NTIME, and 'around' puts W ('start of weekend') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Time spent off work or idle is a slack, relaxed stretch, hence the question mark on the loose phrasing.

clue.text: See supporting extremists in dispute: autocratic type

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so the verb for see comes below
extremists in takes the end letters of the following word

parts.note: to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: Seeing extremists backing a dispute, a tyrant emerges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists in dispute' gives DE; 'supporting' puts SPOT below it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant with absolute power is an autocrat, so the person is an autocratic sort.

clue.text: Word I supply to encapsulate eccentric principally?

definitions.text: Word I supply to encapsulate eccentric principally?

indicators.note: to encapsulate says the shuffled letters close round the next letter
supply read as supple-y, i.e. in a pliable way, so the letters bend into a new order
principally points to the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A request for a word that sums up an eccentric person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' (supple-ly) rearranges WORDI into W_IRDO; 'to encapsulate' holds E, the start of 'eccentric'. Read whole, the clue asks for a word for an eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddball or crank is an eccentric person, which is just the word the clue asks for.

clue.text: Bring up religious books and film as subject

indicators.note: bring up in a down clue means lift the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament
a pic is an informal word for a film

explanation.surface: Raising scripture and cinema as a discussion topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' reverses OT to TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme or matter under discussion is a synonym of subject.

clue.text: A lot about leader of right-wing party in female novelist

indicators.note: about says the word for a lot goes round the next pieces

parts.note: much means a lot

indicators.note: leader of takes the opening letter of right-wing

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A lot of fuss about a right-wing leader in a woman writer's book.
explanation.walkthrough: MU(R + DO)CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch was an Irish-born British woman writer, author of The Sea, the Sea.

clue.text: Garden tools in section of a deck

definitions.meaning: one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: Garden implements stored somewhere on a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the digging implement and the black card suit.

clue.text: Republican bound by agreement I term not quite feasible

indicators.note: bound by means held inside, so the letter goes within the word for agreement

parts.note: a pact is an agreement

indicators.note: not quite drops the final letter

parts.note: to call is to name or term something

explanation.surface: A Republican constrained by an agreement concedes a term is barely workable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims CALL to CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something workable in practice is realistic and can be done, which is what feasible means.

clue.text: Odd patrol behind rear of crowd making percussive sound

indicators.note: behind says the next pieces come after that letter
rear of takes the last letter of crowd

parts.note: rum is old-fashioned British slang for odd
a beat is a police officer's patrol route

explanation.surface: A strange patrol trailing a crowd while drums sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is a dated British word meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhythmic strike of a drum is a percussive sound.

clue.text: Condition in Asian region, it's said, and European capital

indicators.note: it's said tells us to hear the word rather than see it

parts.note: Sind is a province of Pakistan
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A medical state discovered in a region of Asia and in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: Sind (Sindh) is a province of southern Pakistan; spoken, it gives SYND.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of symptoms forming a recognised medical disorder is a condition.

clue.text: Evasive — like a mule?

definitions.meaning: a mule is a backless slipper, so something resembling one is jokingly slipper-ish

explanation.surface: Someone dodgy is compared to a stubborn animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The mule is not the animal but the backless shoe; adding -Y to the shoe word makes the joke adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A shifty person who avoids being pinned down is called hard to grasp in this way; the second sense is a whimsical coinage from footwear.

clue.text: Body noted for rings gives a second backing performance

indicators.note: backing tells us the letters for a second are written in reverse order

parts.note: A plus S, the abbreviation for second
a turn is an act or performance on stage

explanation.surface: Someone stepping in for a second backing performance on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns AS into SA.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth planet is the celestial body most famous for its ring system.

clue.text: Excuse accepted by couple amazingly

indicators.note: accepted by says the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A couple are surprised to have an excuse accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an appeal or justification offered, as when claiming an excuse.

clue.text: Traditional works sold by companion with retired gents?

indicators.note: works as a verb means the letters of sold are worked into a new order

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the gents is a British name for a men's lavatory, a loo

explanation.surface: Antiques sold by a companion to elderly retired gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' turns SOLD into OLDS; 'retired' reverses LOO into OOL. The gents is a British term for a men's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conservative and attached to older ways is described with this phrase, from the idea of an earlier generation's schooling.

clue.text: Take minute out of wood in river

indicators.note: take ... out of tells us to remove a letter from the word for wood

parts.note: timber is wood for building

explanation.surface: A timeless instruction to spend a minute among the trees by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take ... out of' removes M from TIMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the river that flows through Rome.

clue.text: Parking put by very large hotel that's top-class

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for very large
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A car park beside a vast, luxurious hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing-size label meaning very large.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart or upper-class things are called this in informal British speech.

clue.text: Aim to be free of prejudice?

explanation.surface: A goal of being unbiased.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a goal and an adjective for impartial.

clue.text: Praise a demand in speech

indicators.note: in speech says we hear the words rather than see them written

parts.note: a claim is a demand for something owed

explanation.surface: Someone requests praise out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a claim' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiastic public approval is a synonym for praise.

clue.text: Doctor likes list I put out — showing range of abilities

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
put out says the letter I is left out of the shuffled pool

explanation.surface: A doctor's list of likes, displaying broad competence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges LIKESLIST, and 'I put out' drops one I from the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The full suite of competences a person has is their repertoire of capabilities.

clue.text: Idle sort has to carry gallon in half of Italian island

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the half island name
half of keeps the first four of the island's eight letters

parts.note: Sardinia is a large Italian island in the Mediterranean
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: A lazy person must haul a gallon around Sardinia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives SARD, which holds LUG and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy, sluggish person is an idle sort.

clue.text: Having a complaint, woman in Kentucky is a misery

indicators.note: in tells us the next pieces go inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for the US state
having an illness or complaint means being sick
Jo is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An ailing woman in Kentucky is unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a misery' is a British informal noun for a gloomy person who spoils things.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket who dampens others' fun is called a misery in British usage.

clue.text: English is excluded in long tale

indicators.note: is excluded says the letter for English is removed

parts.note: to long for is to yearn

explanation.surface: English is left out of a long story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambling story, often embellished, is a tale.

clue.text: Assured piece of topical mimicry

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A confident snippet of satirical impersonation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being composed and unflustered is a synonym for being self-assured.

clue.text: Medical case in part of spacecraft

definitions.meaning: a soluble shell containing a dose of medicine
a detachable crew module of a spacecraft

explanation.surface: A medical kit packed into a section of spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a pill casing and a sealed crew module.

clue.text: Arab arranged to tour Arizona in charitable fair

indicators.note: to tour means going round, so the shuffled letters surround the state code
arranged means the letters of Arab are put in a new order

parts.note: AZ is the postal abbreviation for Arizona

explanation.surface: An Arab organises a tour of Arizona for a charity sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tour' is the container signal: the scrambled Arab goes round the state code, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A fund-raising sale of goods for a good cause is a fair of this kind.

clue.text: Jeer abusively man, clerk that's awkward right away

parts.note: he stands for a man

indicators.note: awkward signals the letters are jumbled
right away means the letter R is taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: A man and an awkward clerk shouting insults immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but drops R from CLERK; 'awkward' jumbles the remaining CLEK into CKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrupt a speaker with taunts is to barrack or jeer abusively.

clue.text: Man serving in pub dispensing a litre shows reason

indicators.note: in says the soldier sits inside the shortened word for pub
dispensing with means doing without, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: a local is a British term for one's neighbourhood pub
a GI is an American soldier, a serving man

explanation.surface: A barman serving in a pub skimps on a litre, which shows good reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispensing' removes A and L from LOCAL to leave LOC. A local is a British neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational thinking or sound argument is a synonym for reasoning.

clue.text: Put another way, bore apt to follow first signs of roguish excess?

definitions.text: Put another way, bore apt to follow first signs of roguish excess?

indicators.note: to follow says the shuffled letters come after the initials
first signs of takes the opening letter of each of the next two words
put another way means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull person tends to follow early hints of roguish indulgence.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue paints a dissolute rogue, so it works as both definition and wordplay; 'bore apt' looks like a person but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An unprincipled rogue given to excess is exactly a scoundrel of this kind, so the whole clue describes one.

clue.text: Priest upset in excessive amount becomes tipsy

indicators.note: in says the reversed priest sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: OD is an overdose, an excessive amount

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest knocked over by too much drink ends up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ELI into ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly drunk is a slang sense of the word, as with well-lubricated.

clue.text: Return of help at small sports venues

indicators.note: return of tells us to read the following pieces backwards

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Help returning to small sports grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' turns AIDATS into STADIA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin plural of the word for a sports arena.

clue.text: Use authority wrongly to withdraw facility for taxis

parts.note: to pull something out is to withdraw it
a rank is a place where taxis wait for fares

explanation.surface: An official closes the taxi stand by abusing power.
explanation.walkthrough: A rank (taxi rank) is the British term for a taxi stand.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means exploiting a senior position to get one's way unfairly.

clue.text: More organised inspector enters area of stand

indicators.note: enters says the inspector goes inside the word for the seating area

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats in a grandstand
DI is Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A police inspector arrives in the grandstand, which is better arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Neater and better kept is the comparative of tidy, matching more organised.

clue.text: Representative of order and greed man unleashed

indicators.note: unleashed means let loose, so the letters run free into a new order

explanation.surface: A greedy man let loose on the forces of law and order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unleashed' rearranges GREEDMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A French police officer is an agent of law and order.
